species.name: Bluegill
species.blurb: Worms on the flats. A sweet fillet, and they keep a line busy.

species.name: Yellow bullhead
species.blurb: Small cat, big mouth. Dusk, worms, and skinny water.

species.name: Black crappie
species.blurb: Papermouth. Minnows at dawn around brush and lilies.

species.name: Common carp
species.blurb: They will pull a jug under. Worms on the warm flats.

species.name: Freshwater drum
species.blurb: Croaker. Crawfish and cut bait over deep mud.

species.name: Channel catfish
species.blurb: The lake's wage. Liver at night along cypress and the creek.

species.name: Blue catfish
species.blurb: The big one. Cut shad, the deep hole, after dark.

species.name: Flathead catfish
species.blurb: They want it alive. Minnows on the south rocks at night.

species.name: Largemouth bass
species.blurb: A bass will take a trotline minnow at dawn in the lilies.

species.name: Smallmouth bass
species.blurb: Bronze and mean. Crawfish along the south rocks.

species.name: Longnose gar
species.blurb: Long teeth. Cut bait in the cypress after sunset.

species.name: Smallmouth buffalo
species.blurb: A deep-water drifter. Not prized, but they fill a well.

species.name: White crappie
species.blurb: Minnows beside brush and creek channels. Cedar Creek's other papermouth.

species.name: Redear sunfish
species.blurb: Shellcracker. Worms and small crawfish on a firm, shallow bottom.

species.name: Green sunfish
species.blurb: A hungry little creek fish. Worms near rocks and flooded banks.

species.name: Warmouth
species.blurb: Big mouth, small fish. Minnows and worms in brushy coves.

species.name: Redbreast sunfish
species.blurb: Long ear flap and a copper belly. Worms in creek mouths.

species.name: Longear sunfish
species.blurb: Bright colors in clear shallows. Worms along rocky banks.

species.name: Spotted bass
species.blurb: A creek-channel hunter. Minnows or crawfish around rock and drops.

species.name: White bass
species.blurb: Schooling sand bass. Minnows where the creek channel meets open water.

species.name: Yellow bass
species.blurb: Golden schooling bass. Small minnows over submerged humps.

species.name: Hybrid striped bass
species.blurb: Cedar Creek's stocked powerhouse. Shad and minnows over deep humps.

species.name: Striped bass
species.blurb: A rare Little Briar stocking. Cut shad in deep, open water.

species.name: Bowfin
species.blurb: An old swamp predator. Cut bait in warm, weedy backwaters.

species.name: Spotted gar
species.blurb: A spotted ambush fish. Shad and minnows beside flooded timber.

species.name: Shortnose gar
species.blurb: A short, broad snout. Cut bait near muddy creek mouths.

species.name: Alligator gar
species.blurb: The heavyweight. Cut shad in creek channels; a big one needs a big well.

species.name: Black bullhead
species.blurb: A small cat from quiet, muddy water. Liver or worms after dark.

species.name: Brown bullhead
species.blurb: A mottled Little Briar catfish. Liver beside flooded brush.

species.name: Blue sucker
species.blurb: A rare channel-bottom visitor in Little Briar. Worms on deeper gravel.

species.name: Bigmouth buffalo
species.blurb: A broad-backed drifter. An occasional worm catch over deep mud.

species.name: Black buffalo
species.blurb: A scarce Little Briar bottom fish. Worms or cut bait on the deep shelf.

species.name: Golden shiner
species.blurb: A flashing gold forage fish. Tiny worm bites among the weeds.

species.name: Gizzard shad
species.blurb: Broad schools over open water. An occasional small worm catch.

species.name: Threadfin shad
species.blurb: A tiny forage fish, rarely caught on a baited hook. Warm open water.

species.name: Chain pickerel
species.blurb: A toothy Little Briar weed hunter. Live minnows in the lily cove.

species.name: Inland silverside
species.blurb: Glass Sliver is see-through and shy of nothing. Open water, worms.

species.name: Bluntnose minnow
species.blurb: Button-Nose crowds the creek channels. Worms or dough.

species.name: River carpsucker
species.blurb: The Silver Vacuum cleans the creek bottom. Dough balls work.

species.name: Orangespotted sunfish
species.blurb: Ember-Dot glows in the flooded shoreline. Worms by day.

species.name: Bigscale logperch
species.blurb: Log-Roller flips pebbles on the dam riprap. Worms.

species.name: Bullhead minnow
species.blurb: Little Boss rules the channels at dusk. Worms.

species.name: Lake trout
species.blurb: The Deep Mackinaw follows the cold down and down. Minnows at dawn.

species.name: Bull trout
species.blurb: Old Bull comes up the inlets at dawn. If you meet one, let it go home.

species.name: Westslope cutthroat trout
species.blurb: Red-Throat loves the inlet riffles. Worms by day.

species.name: Rainbow trout
species.blurb: Sky-Side rises in the inlets and pondweed bay. Dough works too.

species.name: Brook trout
species.blurb: Speckle is shy and lives in the snowmelt inlet. A quiet boat helps.

species.name: Brown trout
species.blurb: Butter-Belly lurks by the larch snags at dusk. Minnow or craw.

species.name: Kokanee salmon
species.blurb: Silver Bullets school out deep at dawn. Roe, always roe.

species.name: Lake whitefish
species.blurb: Snow-Belly grazes the trench bottom. Worms or roe.

species.name: Mountain whitefish
species.blurb: Pebble-Nose sniffs the inlet stones by day.

species.name: Pygmy whitefish
species.blurb: Thimble lives so deep it's practically a rumor. Night, worms.

species.name: Northern pike
species.blurb: The Water Wolf waits in the pondweed with its teeth out.

species.name: Yellow perch
species.blurb: Tiger-Stripes crowd the pondweed bay and the outpost dock.

species.name: Burbot
species.blurb: The Eelpout comes up at night on the gravel reefs. It's all chin.

species.name: Largescale sucker
species.blurb: Rubber-Lip vacuums the inlet. Dough balls.

species.name: Longnose sucker
species.blurb: Snoot keeps to the cold reefs.

species.name: Peamouth
species.blurb: Pea-Pods dimple the bay at dusk.

species.name: Northern pikeminnow
species.blurb: The Big-Mouth Minnow is no minnow at all. Gravel reefs, dusk.

species.name: Redside shiner
species.blurb: Sunset Flicker flashes pink over the flats.

species.name: Slimy sculpin
species.blurb: Puddle-Puss hides under reef stones on cold nights.

species.name: Mottled sculpin
species.blurb: Patchwork sits so still you'd think it was a pebble.

species.name: Lake chub
species.blurb: Button pops up anywhere shallow. Dough.

species.name: Pumpkinseed
species.blurb: Penny-Cheek suns itself by the outpost dock.

species.name: Cisco
species.blurb: Lake Herring flash in the open water at dawn.

species.name: Arctic grayling
species.blurb: Sail-Fin only shows itself to quiet boats in the inlet.

species.name: Golden trout
species.blurb: Sunbeam lives in the snowmelt shallows. Shy as morning.

species.name: Tiger trout
species.blurb: Marble-Back prowls the reefs at dusk. Minnows.

species.name: Splake
species.blurb: Twice-Char can't decide what it is, but it likes deep reefs at dawn.

species.name: Longnose dace
species.blurb: Riffle-Nose noses the inlet stones. Worms.

species.name: Mountain sucker
species.blurb: Cobble-Kiss kisses every stone in the inlet.

species.name: White sturgeon
species.blurb: The Old Plates is older than the outpost. Deep, at night. Let it go.

species.name: Walleye
species.blurb: Glass-Eye sees in the dark. Reefs at dusk, minnows.

species.name: Sauger
species.blurb: Sand-Eye follows the cold into the trench at night.

species.name: Shorthead redhorse
species.blurb: Rusty Tail flicks red in the inlet. Worms or craw.

species.name: Fathead minnow
species.blurb: Pudge is everyone's snack. Dough by the dock.

species.name: Redband trout
species.blurb: Ember-Stripe warms itself by the springs. Worms or grubs.

species.name: Coastal cutthroat trout
species.blurb: Rain-Throat hides among the drowned pines at dawn. Quiet boats.

species.name: Lahontan cutthroat trout
species.blurb: The Desert King is rare and royal. Deep at dawn. Let it go.

species.name: Chinook salmon
species.blurb: King's Supper roams the cobalt deep at dawn. Roe.

species.name: Coho salmon
species.blurb: Silver-Side flashes in the open caldera at dawn.

species.name: Tui chub
species.blurb: Button-Belly loafs on the pumice shelf.

species.name: Speckled dace
species.blurb: Freckle dances in the warm spring shallows.

species.name: Oregon chub
species.blurb: Moss Pip hides in the moss gardens. Shy, worms.

species.name: Klamath smallscale sucker
species.blurb: Soft-Mouth grazes the shelf and the deep. Dough.

species.name: Blue chub
species.blurb: Bluebell rings near the surface in the moss gardens.

species.name: Prickly sculpin
species.blurb: Pincushion bristles under the cliffs at night.

species.name: Umpqua pikeminnow
species.blurb: River Wolf hunts the drowned pines at dusk.

species.name: Chiselmouth
species.blurb: Scraper scrapes the cliff stones by day.

species.name: Alvord chub
species.blurb: Dust Pip lives only in the warmest springs. Grubs.

species.name: Cobalt cisco
species.blurb: The Blue Ghost lives where the water is bluest. Deep, dawn.

species.name: Obsidian darter
species.blurb: Glass Bead darts along the obsidian. Grubs.

species.name: Ember char
species.blurb: Coal-Belly glows a little at dusk near the springs.

species.name: Ash minnow
species.blurb: Smudge is grey as ash and everywhere on the shelf.

species.name: Cinder sculpin
species.blurb: Hot-Rock sits on warm stones at night.

species.name: Pumice skipper
species.blurb: Bobber-Fish floats like pumice. Dough at the surface.

species.name: Fumarole perch
species.blurb: Steam-Stripe loves the springs by day.

species.name: Sulfur shiner
species.blurb: Yellow Spark flickers in the spring water.

species.name: Basalt bass
species.blurb: Black Brick guards the cliffs at dawn. Crawfish.

species.name: Glasswing trout
species.blurb: Window-Fin is see-through on clear days in the open.

species.name: Mistfin dace
species.blurb: Fog-Flicker only comes out when the fog does.

species.name: Lava-belly sunfish
species.blurb: Hot Penny glows orange in the spring shallows.

species.name: Geyser goby
species.blurb: Hiccup hops near the springs at night.

species.name: Moonpool whitefish
species.blurb: Night-Lamp rises in the deep after dark.

species.name: Snagtooth pike
species.blurb: Old Crook-Jaw waits in the drowned pines at dusk.

species.name: Fog mudminnow
species.blurb: Hide-Away hides even better in fog.

species.name: Indigo eelpout
species.blurb: Velvet Rope lives deeper than the light goes. Night, cut shad.

species.name: Steam carp
species.blurb: Kettle-Lips blows bubbles in the springs. Dough.

species.name: Rimrock bullhead
species.blurb: Pebble-Whisker pokes around the cliffs at night. Liver.

species.name: Vent catfish
species.blurb: Warm-Whiskers naps by the deep springs and wakes at night for liver.

species.name: Comet minnow
species.blurb: Tail-Lights zip up the comet stream. Star-dust.

species.name: Meteor bass
species.blurb: Rock-Drop crashes into the meteor reefs at rising.

species.name: Quasar koi
species.blurb: Lantern Koi glow in the lily drifts. Dough or star-dust.

species.name: Pulsar perch
species.blurb: Blinkers blink in the deep phase. Count the blinks.

species.name: Lunar loach
species.blurb: Moon-Noodle wiggles through the light-reeds at night.

species.name: Solar sunfish
species.blurb: Little Sun warms the lily drifts in the bright phase.

species.name: Starling shiner
species.blurb: Twinkle-Fry flock in the light-reeds at fading.

species.name: Galaxy gar
species.blurb: Swirl-Snout spirals in the current at fading.

species.name: Aurora trout
species.blurb: Ribbon-Light shimmers in the comet stream at rising. Roe.

species.name: Cosmic carp
species.blurb: Big Bubble blows bubbles shaped like planets.

species.name: Void eel
species.blurb: Long Shadow lives in the void well. Liver, deep phase.

species.name: Orbit bluegill
species.blurb: Ring-Gills circle the station dock.

species.name: Gravity drum
species.blurb: Thumpers thump in the deep. You feel it in the hull.

species.name: Photon tetra
species.blurb: Sparks light up the reeds at night.

species.name: Nova pike
species.blurb: Flare-Jaw flares in the crystal kelp at fading.

species.name: Dwarf-star darter
species.blurb: Speck is tiny, bright and lives on the meteor reefs.

species.name: Saturnfin puffer
species.blurb: Ring-Ball floats in the current with its fins like rings.

species.name: Celestial catfish
species.blurb: Star-Whiskers prowls the void well at night. Liver.

species.name: Moonbeam crappie
species.blurb: Paper-Moon hides in the crystal kelp at rising.

species.name: Twinkle shad
species.blurb: Glitter-Fry schools in the current. Star-dust.

species.name: Eclipse bowfin
species.blurb: Half-Moon lurks in the reeds at night.

species.name: Stardust bullhead
species.blurb: Sprinkle-Cat noses the shoals at night. Liver or worms.

species.name: Asteroid sucker
species.blurb: Pock-Lip grazes the meteor reefs.

species.name: Halo whitefish
species.blurb: Ring-Light rises in the open at rising. Roe.

species.name: Constellation char
species.blurb: Dot-to-Dot follows the current at fading. Connect its spots.

species.name: Milky-way buffalo
species.blurb: Cream-Back drifts over the shoals.

species.name: Supernova salmon
species.blurb: Burst only bites for the patient, in the current at rising.

species.name: Event-horizon goby
species.blurb: The Edge-Sitter sits at the very bottom of the void well.

species.name: Zodiac zander
species.blurb: Twelve-Stripe has a stripe for every month. Reefs at fading.

species.name: Plasma pickerel
species.blurb: Zap-Jaw zaps in the reeds at rising. Minnows.

species.name: Ion icefish
species.blurb: Clear-Cat is invisible except at night, deep in the current.

species.name: Prism ray
species.blurb: Rainbow Kite glides over the shoals on bright days.

species.name: Comet-tail betta
species.blurb: Silk-Tail flutters at the surface of the lily drifts.

species.name: Purrsec lanternfish
species.blurb: Purr-Lights purr. You can hear them if you're quiet.
